info.title: OpenAsy Supply Chain API
info.summary: What CI knows about every image, and a policy that says which may run.
info.description:
Every screen of supply-chain uses this API, and so can your scripts, CI and admission webhook (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

CI sends what it knows about an image (SBOM, the result of its own signature check, a provenance summary) with `SUPPLY_CHAIN_INGEST_TOKEN`. **This product records what CI says; it does not verify signatures itself** (ADR 0043). Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

post.description:
Stores what CI knows about an image: an SBOM, the result of its own `cosign verify` and a provenance summary. Any of them; what is not sent stays as it was, and a new SBOM replaces the old one. **This product records what CI says. It does not verify signatures or provenance itself** (ADR 0043), so the token that can send evidence is trusted like the pipeline that holds it.

```bash
digest=$(crane digest ghcr.io/acme/app:1.4.2)
syft ghcr.io/acme/app@$digest -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json
cosign verify ghcr.io/acme/app@$digest --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/acme/' --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com >/dev/null && verified=true || verified=false
jq -n --slurpfile sbom sbom.json --argjson verified $verified '{sbom: $sbom[0], signature: {verified: $verified}}' |
  curl -sf -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPPLY_CHAIN_INGEST_TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- \
  "https://supply-chain.example.com/api/v1/images?name=ghcr.io/acme/app&digest=$digest"
```

The body may be gzipped (`Content-Encoding: gzip`), up to 128 MiB unpacked.

Takes SUPPLY_CHAIN_INGEST_TOKEN, or an API token with the editor role.

parameters.description: Only images the policy allows or denies right now.

get.summary: Ask whether an image may run
get.description:
For a Kubernetes admission webhook or a pipeline gate. The answer follows the policy of the moment and the exceptions that have not ended.

Takes SUPPLY_CHAIN_INGEST_TOKEN, or any API token or session (viewer role).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The image without tag or digest, such as `ghcr.io/acme/app`.

200.description: The answer. `allowed` is false for an image nobody reported on.
The image with its reasons and licences.

204.description: Deleted with its SBOM and packages.

200.description: The SBOM as it was sent. The format is in `x-sbom-format`.

get.description:
Searches every stored SBOM, for example when a library is found to be vulnerable.

Needs the viewer role.

200.description: One row per image and version.
The rules every image must meet.

put.description:
Takes the whole policy; fields it does not know are refused, so a typo cannot loosen a rule. It applies to every image at once.

Needs the admin role.

post.summary: Waive a rule for an image
post.description:
Waives one rule, or all, for an image name or one digest, until it ends. It shows up in the answer as waived.

Needs the editor role.

200.description: From OPENASY_PRODUCTS, for the product switcher.
Metrics in the Prometheus text format.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when supply-chain runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the supply-chain origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_supply-chain_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when supply-chain is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

ingestToken.description: `SUPPLY_CHAIN_INGEST_TOKEN`: for CI and the admission webhook. It can send evidence and ask whether an image may run, nothing else.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

waived.description: True when an active exception covers it.

allowed.description: True when nothing is left that the policy has against it, after exceptions.

signature.description: What CI reported about its own signature check. Not verified again here.

provenance.description: What CI reported. Not verified again here.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

licences.description: Every licence expression in the SBOM with how many packages carry it, judged by the policy.

sbom.description: A CycloneDX or SPDX JSON SBOM, as Syft or Trivy write it.

signature.description: The result of `cosign verify`, run by CI.

provenance.description: A summary of the SLSA provenance CI checked.

Check.description: An image nobody reported on is denied, with the reason unknown-image.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.
Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

allowedIdentities.description: Regular expressions; the signer's identity must match one. Empty: any identity.

licenceAllow.description: SPDX ids. Empty: any licence that is not denied. With a list, a package whose licence nobody named is denied.

licenceDeny.description: SPDX ids. An OR expression passes when one alternative does; an AND needs every part.

name.description: The image without tag or digest.

digest.description: Only this build. Without it, every digest of the name.
